name: Zacchaeus
title: The Repentant Tax Collector
summary: Zacchaeus was a tax collector in Jericho known for his wealth and collaboration with the Romans. When Jesus passed through the town, Zacchaeus climbed up into a sycamore-fig tree to see him, and Jesus called him down and visited his home. The encounter with Jesus led to a radical conversion where Zacchaeus promised to give half of his possessions to the poor and repay fourfold anyone he had cheated.

keyEvents.title: Zacchaeus Climbs a Tree
keyEvents.description: Zacchaeus was short in stature and could not see Jesus through the crowd, so he climbed up into a sycamore-fig tree along the road where Jesus was to pass.

keyEvents.title: Jesus Calls Zacchaeus Down
keyEvents.description: Jesus looked up into the tree, called Zacchaeus by name, and said that he must stay at his house that day. Zacchaeus came down quickly and welcomed Jesus joyfully.

keyEvents.title: The Crowd Murmurs
keyEvents.description: When the people saw that Jesus was going to the home of a sinner and tax collector, they murmured and criticized Jesus for associating with such a man.

keyEvents.title: Zacchaeus's Conversion and Promise
keyEvents.description: Zacchaeus stood up and promised to give half of what he owned to the poor, and to repay fourfold everyone he had cheated out of money.

keyEvents.title: Jesus Declares Salvation Over the House
keyEvents.description: Jesus declared that salvation had come to this house, because Zacchaeus was also a son of Abraham. Jesus emphasized that the Son of Man came to seek and save what was lost.
